key_takeaways: The long-standing convention is that everyone invited to the shower is also invited to the wedding, so draw the shower list from the wedding list.
The host draws up the list and sends the invitations, and the bride supplies the names and approves them; our advice is to give each mother the same set number of places.
Apply one test to both families, for cousins, aunts and family friends alike, so nobody on either side feels left out.
For a destination wedding, a shower at home lets invited guests who cannot travel share in the lead-up, and a video link can bring in anyone overseas.
The shower and the hens are separate events with separate guest lists.

faq.q: Do you have to invite everyone from the bridal shower to the wedding?
faq.a: Yes, by long-standing convention. Everyone invited to the shower is also invited to the wedding, because a shower invitation implies a wedding one and comes with the expectation of a gift. Colleagues who are not coming to the wedding can celebrate separately at work.

faq.q: Can you invite someone to the bridal shower who is not invited to the wedding?
faq.a: It is best avoided, because a shower invitation implies a wedding one and a guest can feel asked for a present but not the day itself. If someone you love is not on the wedding list, a relaxed afternoon tea after the wedding with no gifts expected is one kind option.

faq.q: How many people should be on a bridal shower guest list?
faq.a: There is no set number. The wedding list sets the ceiling, so a small wedding means a smaller shower. An afternoon tea at home is sized by the living room, a hotel high tea by the booking, and a winery or spa day suits a smaller group.

faq.q: Who makes the bridal shower guest list?
faq.a: The host draws it up and sends the invitations, and the bride or her family supplies the names, with the bride approving the final list. Give each mother the same set number of places, so both sides are treated alike.

faq.q: Should you have a bridal shower if many guests cannot travel to the wedding?
faq.a: Often, yes. A shower at home lets the people who cannot travel share in the lead-up without a flight, a hotel and time off work. Hold the shower in Australia before you fly out, leaving enough time to post any gifts on.
